idiom_name: expires_at field plus clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) check before dispatch
implementation_notes: C has no runtime facility for message expiry, so the receiver hand-builds the mechanism: the message struct carries an absolute deadline in monotonic milliseconds and the consumer compares clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) against it before doing any work. A bounded blocking receive can be built with pthread_cond_timedwait, whose abstime argument is an absolute deadline, but the condition variable must be created with pthread_condattr_setclock(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - otherwise it waits on the settable CLOCK_REALTIME and a clock step can wake the consumer early or hold it past its deadline. Because a monotonic origin is per-boot and meaningless to peers, the value on the wire must be an absolute wall-clock timestamp (CLOCK_REALTIME or TIME_UTC) that each hop converts once into its local monotonic deadline.
pitfalls: CLOCK_REALTIME is settable: a TTL computed from it silently changes when NTP steps or an operator sets the clock. Derive local deadlines from CLOCK_MONOTONIC and convert only at the wire boundary.

pthread_cond_timedwait waits on CLOCK_REALTIME unless the condition variable was created with pthread_condattr_setclock(CLOCK_MONOTONIC), and its abstime is absolute - recomputing it inside the wait loop is a classic source of hangs.
Without a broker enforcing TTL, an unconsumed queue grows without bound; the dequeue check only protects messages that are actually consumed, and a priority heap of deadlines must still be swept.
